appstore-full.en:
Rún is a secure messenger built for people who refuse to compromise on privacy. Every message is end-to-end encrypted before it leaves your device, and the keys ratchet forward as you chat — so even if one key were ever exposed, the rest of the conversation stays sealed.

Rún requires no account, no phone number, and no email address. There is nothing to link back to your identity. Contacts are added in person by scanning QR codes, or through a vouched introduction from someone you already trust — no central directory, no contact discovery, no social graph.

All traffic is routed through the Tor network, hiding your IP address and location even from Rún's own relay. An observer monitoring your network sees only encrypted Tor traffic — they cannot tell who you are talking to or what you are saying. Messages are padded to fixed sizes, so not even the length of a message leaks.

Messages live in memory only — they are never written to disk. Leave a chat or close the app, and they are gone. There is no message history to scroll through, no archive to subpoena, and no backup to leak. The relay stores only temporary encrypted blobs it cannot read, in inboxes that expire on their own.

Your vault is encrypted at rest with AES-256 via SQLCipher, its key derived with Argon2id and protected by the device keychain, tied to this device only. You choose how hard it is to reach:

• Decent — quick PIN unlock, with relaxed auto-lock and self-wipe timers.
• Secure — the vault key is also bound to the Secure Enclave, behind Face ID or Touch ID. A seized phone strongly resists offline attacks.
• Maximum — the PIN is replaced by a strong passphrase and the timers are at their tightest. Even a fully imaged phone stays shut.

At every level Rún locks itself when idle, wipes after too many wrong unlock attempts, and self-destructs after a long stretch of inactivity — how strict is set by the level you choose. A wipe erases the encryption keys themselves, leaving nothing recoverable.

Group chats live only on their members' phones — no group account, no member list. Each message goes privately to every member: the relay sees one message reach several inboxes, never who they are or a word of it.

No analytics. No tracking. No advertising. No crash reporting. No cloud backups. By default it stays silent — no notifications — and you simply see your messages when you open the app. You can optionally turn notifications on; if you do, a content-free wake-up signal routes through Apple's push servers, which learn only that something arrived and when — never who it is from or what it says — and Rún tells you exactly this before you enable it.

The client's source code is public under the GPL at github.com/cptdad/run: read it, build it yourself, or report a security issue there. The relay server is not published yet.

Rún is built for journalists, activists, whistleblowers, and anyone who believes private conversation is a fundamental right.

Key features:
- End-to-end encryption with forward secrecy (AES-256-GCM + Double Ratchet)
- All traffic over Tor — your IP and location stay hidden
- No account, phone number, or email required
- In-person QR contact exchange and vouched introductions
- Group chats with no group account or member list
- Messages held in memory only — never stored on disk
- Encrypted local vault (SQLCipher, Argon2id, device keychain)
- Three protection levels: Decent, Secure, Maximum
- Auto-lock, wipe on repeated wrong attempts, self-destruct on inactivity
- No analytics, tracking, ads, or crash reporting
- Move phones with a sealed transfer, never a cloud backup
- Available in 13 languages

play-short.en: Anonymous, end-to-end encrypted messenger over Tor. No accounts. No traces.

whatsnew.en:
• Maximum: a song line typed without spaces no longer passes as a strong passphrase.
• Groups: a text that missed members says "not delivered to N"; leaving warns that unread texts may be lost.
• Locks can't be postponed; showing a move code again asks you to unlock.
• Tighter keyboard and clipboard privacy.
• A cancelled move import no longer gets stuck.
• About links to the source code and lists the licences.

about_contacts_body.en: No emails, no sign-ups — and no stranger can add you. You meet in person and scan each other's QR. Each contact gets a random codename; add a private note only you can see, so only you know who they really are.

about_e2e_body.en: Every message is sealed with a key only you and your contact hold, and as you keep chatting that key ratchets forward — so exposing a single key still leaves the rest sealed.

about_forensic_body.en: A seized phone gives up nothing useful. Everything at rest is sealed with SQLCipher, and a wipe erases the keys themselves — leaving only noise, no caches or fragments. How hard it is to open is your choice: Decent leans on your PIN; Secure binds the key to this phone's security chip, behind your fingerprint or face; Maximum swaps the PIN for a passphrase only you know — so even a fully imaged phone stays shut.

about_groups_body.en: A group lives only on its members' phones — no group account, no member list, nothing on the relay to seize. Each message is sent privately to every member, so the relay never learns the group's name, who's in it, or a word of what's said. It does see one message go to several inboxes at once — enough to tell a group exists and how many it reached, never whose.

about_info_clearnet_message.en: %1$s opens in your browser over the normal internet — not Tor. The website and your network can see your device's IP address.

about_lockwipe_body.en: Left idle or sent to the background, Rún locks — you unlock again with your PIN or passphrase. Too many wrong tries, or a long stretch untouched, goes further: it erases the keys and all data, beyond recovery. How soon each happens is set by the protection level you choose.

about_quiet_body.en: No ads, analytics, or profiles — ever, and out of the box no notifications: Rún reaches its relay, over Tor, only when you open it. You can opt into instant alerts — a contentless wake carried by Apple's or Google's push service, or by one you install yourself, revealing only rough timing, never the message or who sent it — off unless you turn it on.

about_ready_body.en: That's Rún — quiet, private, and yours to keep secret. Add someone in person, and start a conversation no one else can see. The app's code is public at github.com/cptdad/run, so anyone can read it.

about_referrals_body.en: There's no directory of who's on Rún. Instead, someone you already trust can introduce you to someone they trust — and you choose whether to accept. Trust travels person to person, never through a server.

about_relay_body.en: Rún's relay is deliberately dumb — no accounts, nothing to read, just padded blobs in numbered inboxes it passes along, their padded size revealing nothing about the contents. Nothing lingers once it's delivered — messages clear from the inbox as you read them, and the inbox itself is reclaimed after a long stretch of silence.

about_relay_runestone_body.en: When the ᚱ at its centre burns white, Rún has reached the relay — messages can send and arrive. Red without the white ᚱ means Tor is up but the relay isn't reachable yet.

about_screen_privacy_body_android.en: Screenshots, screen recording, and the recent-apps preview are all blocked, so nothing leaks to your gallery or the app switcher.

about_screen_privacy_body_ios.en: The app-switcher preview and screen recording are covered. iOS can't block a manual screenshot, so take care with sensitive chats — Rún warns you if one is taken.

about_tor_intro_body.en: Everything Rún sends rides Tor — a global network that relays your traffic through several hops, hiding your IP and location. Not even Rún's own relay learns who or where you are, and Rún connects no other way.

about_tor_runestone_body.en: Watch the runestone — red means you're on Tor. Its ring pulses harder the closer you get, holds solid red the moment the relay answers, and then the R lights.

about_vanish_body.en: This is "burn on read": messages live in memory alone, never on disk. Close the app or leave a chat, and they're gone for good.

about_welcome_body.en: Messaging with nothing to seize, trace, or subpoena — no accounts, no numbers, no trail. The name is Old Norse: "rún" — secret, hidden knowledge, the root of "rune", and in Irish and Scottish Gaelic the beloved trusted to keep it.

add_contact_announce_hint.en: They'll be able to message you in a moment — your inbox is delivered automatically.

add_contact_cancel_pairing_message.en: This deletes the half-finished contact and closes its inboxes. You’ll both have to start over with new codes.

add_contact_choice_subtitle.en: You and your contact swap codes. Pick how to start — you’ll do both.

add_contact_inbox_in_use.en: Couldn't add this contact — one of the inboxes in their code is already in use here. If you're re-adding someone you already have, delete the old contact first, then try again.

add_contact_mnemonic_placeholder.en: e.g. Met at the conference in Oslo

add_contact_paste_not_ready.en: Still setting up inbox — try again in a moment

add_contact_scan_back_hint.en: Now let them scan your code. You’ll be able to message each other the moment they do.

add_contact_scan_deadlock.en: Scan the code on their “Almost there” screen

add_contact_show_hint_pending.en: Have them scan this. You’ll scan theirs next.

add_contact_show_hint_scanned.en: Have them scan this, then finish.

burn_notice_message.en: Messages appear once — right here — and are never saved. When you leave this conversation, they are gone for good.

connect_mint_stalled_hint.en: Still connecting… This network may be blocking the private connection. Try different Wi-Fi or mobile data — we’ll keep trying.

connect_relay_first_time_hint.en: The first connection can take a few minutes.

connect_relay_relaunch_hint.en:
The secure connection can’t recover in this session.
Close and reopen Rún to reconnect.

connect_relay_slow_hint.en: Tor network can sometimes be slow, this is the price for total anonymity

connect_relay_stalled_reopen_hint.en:
Still can’t reach the relay.
Reopen Rún if this keeps happening.

connect_tor_reboot_hint.en: If closing and reopening hasn’t helped, restart your iPhone.

connect_tor_stalled_hint.en:
Still connecting…
This network may be blocking the private connection. Try different Wi-Fi or mobile data — we’ll keep trying.

connect_tor_stalled_long_hint.en:
Still can’t connect.
Close Rún completely and open it again — that starts a fresh private connection.

contact_list_block_contact_message.en: You will no longer receive messages from %1$s, and they will be removed from your list.

contact_list_block_shared_groups_message.en: %1$s is still a member of a group you share. Blocking doesn't remove them from it — they'll keep receiving your messages there from every other member. Leave a shared group below, or block %1$s anyway.

contact_list_delete_confirm_message.en: All messages will be permanently destroyed

contact_list_delete_contact_message.en: This will permanently delete this contact and all associated messages.

contact_list_group_invite_mismatch.en: ⚠️ %1$s invited you to “%2$s”, but you previously had this group under a DIFFERENT administrator. Only join if you trust %1$s to control this group’s membership.

contact_list_group_invite_mismatch_with_.en: ⚠️ %1$s invited you to “%2$s”, but you previously had this group under a DIFFERENT administrator (originally administered by “%3$s”). Only join if you trust %1$s to control this group’s membership.

contact_list_leave_group_admin_message_a.en: You are the admin. After you leave, nobody can change the member list.

contact_list_leave_group_admin_message_i.en: You're the group admin. Open the group, tap the info button, and choose a new admin — then you can leave.

contact_list_memory_dialog_subtitle.en: A private reminder of who this contact is. Only you can see this.

contact_list_memory_placeholder_android.en: e.g. Met at the conference in 2025

contact_list_memory_placeholder_ios.en: e.g., Met at the conference in 2025

contact_list_post_block_report_message.en: Would you like to report this contact for objectionable content or abuse? Reports are reviewed and acted on within 24 hours. Your report is sent from your own email app, so it will show us your email address — and the draft is stored by that app, outside Rún, where it won't be erased if you wipe Rún.

contact_list_reset_relay_failure.en: Couldn't reach the relay. Rún will finish this on its own.

contact_list_reset_relay_message.en:
Rún will get new access keys for this conversation from the relay. Your messages, your history and this contact stay exactly as they are, and %1$s doesn't have to do anything.

Do this if you think someone else had your phone while it was unlocked. It can't undo anything they already read — and if the phone really was taken, the safest fix is still to delete this contact and pair again in person.

conversation_fs_stalled_body.en: Messages to this contact are still encrypted, but they don't yet get the extra protection that keeps past messages safe if a key is later exposed. This usually clears once they reply. If it persists, remove and re-add the contact.

conversation_pending_banner.en: Waiting for this contact's inbox — you'll be able to send in a moment.

conversation_ratchet_refused_body.en: Secure channel could not be established with this contact. Messages are not being sent. Remove the contact and pair again.

conversation_report_confirm_message.en: Reports are reviewed and acted on within 24 hours. Your report is sent from your own email app, so it will show us your email address — and the draft is stored by that app, outside Rún, where it won't be erased if you wipe Rún.

conversation_screenshot_warning_banner.en: ⚠ Screenshot saved to Photos — that image is NOT encrypted and can sync to iCloud.

create_group_failed.en: Could not create the group. Check the connection and try again.

create_group_precondition.en: Everyone in a group must have paired in person with everyone else. You are vouching for that when you create it.

debug_mode_message.en: Send anonymous diagnostic logs to the relay to help development. The logs never include anything that identifies you or this device: no names, no message content, no addresses, no keys, no inbox or contact ids.

debug_mode_message_off.en: Debug mode is on. Turn it off to stop sending anonymous diagnostic logs.

donate_appeal.en: Rún has no ads, no investors, and never sells your data. Every donation — large or small — helps keep it free for everyone, forever.

donate_play_disclosure.en: Processed by Google Play · ties to your Google account · no other third party.

eula_body.en:
By using Rún you agree to these Terms of Use.

Rún is a private, end-to-end encrypted messenger. You add contacts in person by exchanging a QR code, and your messages are encrypted on your device before they are sent. We cannot read your messages and we do not host a public feed, profiles, or any shared content.

ZERO TOLERANCE FOR OBJECTIONABLE CONTENT AND ABUSE
There is no tolerance for objectionable, illegal, or abusive content or behaviour on Rún. You agree not to use Rún to send, request, or solicit content that is unlawful, harassing, threatening, hateful, sexually exploitative, or otherwise objectionable, and not to abuse, harass, or harm other people. Violating this is a breach of these terms.

KEEPING YOURSELF SAFE
Because your conversations are private to you and the people you add, you are in control of who can contact you:

• Report — if a contact sends you objectionable content or behaves abusively, use "Report" (in a conversation, or by pressing and holding the contact) to notify us. We review every report within 24 hours and act on it — barring abusive senders where we are technically able to, and reporting illegal content to the appropriate authorities. Because messages are end-to-end encrypted, we act on what you tell us in your report.

• Block — use "Block" to immediately hide a contact so you no longer see them or their messages. Blocking is reversible — you can unblock any time from the settings menu.

You are responsible for the content you send and for the people you choose to add as contacts. You must be old enough to form a binding agreement in your country to use Rún.

NO WARRANTY
Rún is provided "as is", without warranties of any kind, to the fullest extent permitted by law.

Contact: %1$s

eula_decline_alert_message.en: You must accept the Terms of Use to use Rún. They exist to keep everyone safe and forbid objectionable content and abusive behaviour.

ext_proxy_description.en: Send all relay traffic through a SOCKS5 proxy you run, such as Orbot or Tor on your own network, instead of Rún's built-in Tor. While this is on, the built-in Tor never starts. If the proxy can't be reached, Rún stays offline. It never falls back.

ext_proxy_error_host.en: Enter an IP address on this phone or your local network: 127.x.x.x, ::1, 10.x.x.x, 172.16–31.x.x, 192.168.x.x or 169.254.x.x. Host names aren't allowed.

ext_proxy_error_save.en: Couldn't save the setting. Try again.

ext_proxy_lan_warning.en: Traffic between this phone and the proxy is not encrypted. Anyone who can watch or impersonate this address, including on other networks this phone joins later, gets the access tokens to your conversation inboxes. They could delete or take over those inboxes, but can't read your messages. Use this only on a network you control, and turn the mode off when you leave it.

ext_proxy_loopback_warning.en: While the proxy app (such as Orbot) isn't running, any other app on this phone can take its port and receive the same access tokens. Set the proxy app to a non-default port and keep it running.

ext_proxy_next_launch.en: Changes take effect the next time you open Rún.

ext_proxy_saved.en: Saved. Close and reopen Rún to apply it.

ext_proxy_status_invalid.en: External proxy setting is invalid. Fix it in Settings.

ext_proxy_status_unreadable.en: External proxy setting couldn't be read. Messaging is unavailable.

gate_compromised_body.en: This device appears to be rooted. Rún cannot guarantee the security of your messages on a compromised device.

gate_compromised_body_jailbroken.en: This device appears to be jailbroken. Rún cannot guarantee the security of your messages on a compromised device.

gate_passcode_warning_message.en: Rún's at-rest hardware protection is weaker without a device passcode. Set one in Settings for full protection, then return to finish setup. You can continue without one.

group_info_add_member_empty.en: No eligible contacts — everyone you've paired with is already in the group.

group_info_add_member_precondition.en: They must have paired in person with every member. You are vouching for that.

group_info_choose_admin_subtitle_android.en: They'll be able to add and remove members after you leave.

group_info_choose_admin_subtitle_ios.en: Choose who becomes the new admin. They'll be able to add and remove members after you leave.

group_info_leave_confirm_admin_message.en: You are the admin. Transfer the role first, or nobody will be able to change the member list.

group_info_leave_confirm_message.en: The other members will be told you left.

group_info_leave_unread_warning.en: Anything you sent that the others have not read yet may never be shown to them.

group_info_no_verified_pairing.en: No verified pairing with this member yet

group_info_transfer_failed_message.en: Nothing changed — you’re still the admin, so the group stays manageable. Try again.

group_notice_not_delivered.en: Your message did not reach %1$d of the members: not yet reachable from this phone, or the relay refused their copy. Rún keeps no copy to send later.

group_private_from.en: Private from %1$s · only you can see this

infoplist_camera_usage.en: Camera is used to scan QR codes during contact exchange.

infoplist_faceid_usage.en: Face ID unlocks your encrypted vault when hardware-bound unlock is enabled.

infoplist_local_network_usage.en: Local network access is used only when you set an external Tor proxy on your local network.

move_cancel_refused.en: Too late to cancel — the transfer has already been picked up.

move_cancel_unconfirmed.en: Could not check whether the new phone has the transfer yet. Try again in a moment, or wipe this phone once the new one is working.

move_done_body.en: Check the new phone first: it should show your contacts. Once it does, wiping this phone is what makes the move safe — nothing here can be read afterwards.

move_done_expired_hint.en: If the new phone never got it, the code may simply have run out. Keep this phone off and show a fresh code instead.

move_error_already_imported.en: This phone has already taken over a move.

move_error_bad_code.en: That code did not open the transfer. Show the code again on the old phone.

move_error_bundle_gone.en: The transfer is no longer on the relay. Show the code again on the old phone.

move_error_corrupt.en: The transfer could not be read. Show the code again on the old phone.

move_error_generic.en: The move did not work. Try again.

move_error_import.en: Could not finish bringing your data over. Try again.

move_error_locked.en: The vault is not open. Unlock and try again.

move_error_mint.en: Could not prepare the transfer. Try again.

move_error_relay.en: Could not reach the relay. Check your connection and try again.

move_error_schema.en: The old phone runs a newer Rún. Update Rún here, then try again.

move_error_too_large.en: There is too much here to move in one transfer.

move_error_upload.en: The transfer did not upload. Try again.

move_expiry_note.en: The transfer waits on the relay for 30 minutes. After that, show the code again.

move_explain_body.en: Rún packs everything into one sealed transfer and shows you a code. Scan that code on the new phone while you set it up.

move_explain_moves_body.en: Your contacts, your groups, and the keys your conversations run on.

move_explain_stays_body.en: Your recovery code, %1$s protection, and notifications. Set those up again on the new phone.

move_explain_warning.en: This phone stops sending and receiving the moment you start, and stays that way until you wipe it or cancel the move.

move_from_body.en: On the old phone, open the settings menu, tap “Move to new device”, and scan the code it shows.

move_frozen_body.en: A move was started here, so Rún no longer sends or receives on this phone. Show a fresh code to finish the move, cancel to use this phone again, or wipe it.

move_handle_caption.en: Copy this into the new phone if the camera will not cooperate.

move_kept_off_body.en: Rún no longer sends or receives here. Wipe it whenever you are ready.

move_paste_invalid.en: That is not a Rún transfer code.

move_progress_hint.en: Keep Rún open — this runs over Tor and takes a moment.

move_qr_body.en: On the new phone, open Rún, choose “Move from another phone”, and scan this code.

move_qr_title.en: Scan this on the new phone

move_qr_warning.en: Anyone who photographs this code can take the transfer. Show it only to the new phone.

notif_edu_content_safe_deep.en: The wake carries nothing and triggers no network activity by itself. Your messages wait encrypted on the relay until you open Rún, which fetches them over Tor and decrypts them locally with the key derived from your PIN or passphrase. %1$s never receives, stores or relays a single message byte.

notif_edu_content_safe_title.en: Your messages never reach %1$s. Rún fetches them over Tor and decrypts them on this phone only after you unlock.

notif_edu_timing_deep.en: A wake fires each time a message reaches you, so %1$s sees a running pattern — how often, at what hours — tied to this phone’s Rún install. Tor normally hides that timing; turning notifications on trades some of it for instant delivery.

notif_edu_timing_title.en: %1$s only learns when messages reach you — never who sent them or what they say. Over time, those timestamps alone can show when you communicate.

notif_edu_up_content_safe_deep.en: Every wake is encrypted to a key pair that never leaves this phone (Web Push, RFC 8291), so nobody who learns your endpoint can forge a new alert — though your push server could replay one you already received, Rún limits how often a repeat can trigger the banner — and every wake is the same fixed size. Your messages wait encrypted on the relay until you open Rún, which fetches them over Tor and decrypts them locally with the key derived from your PIN or passphrase.

notif_edu_up_content_safe_title.en: Your messages never reach the distributor or its server. Each wake is encrypted to this phone and carries nothing; Rún fetches your messages over Tor and decrypts them after you unlock.

notif_edu_up_distributor_deep.en: The distributor app keeps one connection open to a push server and hands each wake to Rún. Nothing about your messages changes: the wake carries no message, and Rún still fetches and decrypts everything over Tor after you unlock.

notif_edu_up_distributor_title.en: This phone has no Google services, so a separate app you choose — a UnifiedPush distributor such as ntfy — delivers the wake signal.

notif_edu_up_parties_deep.en: That is one party more than the Google build has. The distributor sees every wake because it delivers them; its push server sees them because it forwards them and, on a public server, also sees this phone’s IP address. Neither sees a sender, a message or a count. Tor normally hides that timing; notifications trade some of it for instant delivery. Run your own push server and the second party is you.

notif_edu_up_parties_title.en: Two parties learn when you are contacted — the distributor app and its push server — never who wrote or what. Those timestamps alone can show when you communicate.

notif_edu_vendor_deep.en:
The relay sends a contentless wake through %1$s — no sender, no text, no count — and Rún shows a generic “Notification”. Nothing is fetched or decrypted until you open Rún and unlock. %3$s works the same way; neither vendor is more private.

The relay learns something too: all your inboxes register under the one push address %2$s issued to this phone, so the relay can tell which conversations share a device. Someone able to compel both %2$s and the relay could link you to your conversations. That is why this switch is off until you turn it on.

notif_edu_vendor_title.en: Notifications travel through %1$s’s servers. They never contain your messages — only that a new one is waiting for you.

notif_settings_no_distributor_message.en: This phone has no Google services, so notifications need a UnifiedPush distributor app. Install one — ntfy is the recommended choice — then come back here and turn notifications on.

notif_settings_register_error_distributo.en: Your notification distributor refused the registration. Open it, check it's set up, and try again.
Couldn't connect to your notification distributor. Close Rún fully and reopen it, then try again.

notif_settings_register_error_generic.en: Couldn't register for notifications. Check your connection and try again.

notif_settings_register_error_no_distrib.en: No notification distributor was selected. Install ntfy from F-Droid, then try again.

notif_settings_register_error_no_endpoin.en: Your notification distributor didn't respond in time. Open it, make sure it's connected, and try again.

notif_settings_register_error_vapid_unsu.en: This distributor's push server isn't supported yet — it requires VAPID. ntfy works; you can install it from F-Droid.

notif_settings_sound_hint.en: Alerts sound like any other messenger. Change or silence them in iOS notification settings — Rún never overrides your choice.

notif_settings_sound_row_hint.en: Alerts sound like any other messenger. Change or silence them in Android's notification settings — Rún never overrides your choice.

notif_settings_unregistered_notice.en: Your notification distributor stopped delivering to Rún, so notifications were turned off. Turn them back on to reconnect.

pin_device_key_busy_message.en: Your phone’s secure hardware is busy. Lock your phone, unlock it, and try again.

pin_erase_vault_message.en: The vault on this device cannot be opened — no PIN or passphrase is stored for it. Erasing deletes it permanently and starts a new setup. This cannot be undone.

pin_hardware_lock_not_enabled_message.en: Your phone didn’t confirm the hardware key, so your vault is set up at a lower protection level. You can turn it on later from Settings.

pin_orphaned_vault_notice.en: This device has a vault, but no PIN or passphrase is stored for it, so nothing can open it. Its contents cannot be recovered.

pin_permanent_key_loss_lockscreen_has_re.en: Your device lock screen changed, so the hardware key protecting this vault is gone. Your recovery code can still open it.

pin_permanent_key_loss_lockscreen_no_rec.en: Your device lock screen changed, so the hardware key protecting this vault is gone. Without a recovery code this vault cannot be opened.

pin_permanent_key_loss_passcode_has_reco.en: Your device passcode changed, so the hardware key protecting this vault is gone. Your recovery code can still open it.

pin_permanent_key_loss_passcode_no_recov.en: Your device passcode changed, so the hardware key protecting this vault is gone. Without a recovery code this vault cannot be opened.

pin_setup_passphrase_hint.en: Six or so random words. Typed at every unlock — there is no PIN and no biometric shortcut. That’s the point.

protection_downgrade_message_android.en: Switching to %1$s makes your phone easier to crack if it’s taken. Continue?

protection_downgrade_message_ios.en: Switching to %1$s makes your phone easier to crack if it’s taken.

protection_empty_state.en: Pick a level to continue. No level is chosen for you.

protection_enabling_body_android.en: Your phone may ask you to confirm with its screen lock.

protection_enabling_body_ios.en: Your phone may ask you to confirm with Face ID or its passcode.

protection_forced_explainer_cta_body_and.en: A PIN, pattern, password, or fingerprint all count. Any protection level is available once your phone has one.

protection_forced_explainer_cta_body_ios.en: Open Settings → Face ID & Passcode → Turn Passcode On, then come back to Rún. Any protection level is available once your phone has one.

protection_forced_explainer_intro.en: Without one, the phone itself can't protect Rún's keys — so Rún needs its strongest protection here. Two ways forward:

protection_forced_explainer_outro_androi.en: Or create a passphrase now below — Maximum locks Rún itself, no screen lock needed. Four or five random words make a strong one.

protection_forced_explainer_outro_ios.en: Or create a passphrase now below — Maximum locks Rún itself, no device passcode needed. Four or five random words make a strong one.

protection_forced_notice_body.en:
Without one, your passphrase is the only thing between your messages and anyone holding this phone. So Rún runs at Maximum here.

It asks for that passphrase every time, locks after 60 seconds idle, and the next time Rún is opened after 7 days without use, it erases everything — permanently.

Set a passcode on your phone to choose a gentler level.

protection_lever_b_failed_message.en: Your phone didn't confirm the hardware key, so your vault is set to a lower protection level than you chose. You can try again from Settings.

protection_lever_b_reharden_notice.en: Your protection key needs an upgrade. Turn the Secure tier off and on again to re-harden it.

protection_migration_finish_maximum.en: %1$s needs a passphrase, and this screen doesn't set one — so your vault stays at %2$s for now. To finish, open Settings › Protection level and choose %1$s again — that sets your passphrase and applies its timings.

protection_migration_finish_private.en: We couldn't turn on %1$s's hardware lock here, so your vault stays at %2$s for now. To finish, open Settings › Protection level and choose %1$s again — that turns on the hardware lock and applies its timings.

protection_migration_finish_same.en: %1$s's timings are set now. To finish turning on its stronger unlock, open Settings › Protection level.

protection_persist_failed_message.en: Nothing was changed — the device key was busy. Try again.

protection_recovery_ack_hint_android.en: Tick “I’ve written it down” to continue.

protection_recovery_ack_hint_ios.en: Turn on “I’ve written it down” to continue.

protection_recovery_attempt_record_faile.en: Couldn't record the attempt — the device key is busy. Try again.

protection_recovery_code_body_android.en: Write this down and keep it somewhere safe and separate from your phone. If your fingerprint or device passcode ever changes and locks you out, this code plus your PIN restores your messages. We can't show it again.

protection_recovery_code_body_ios.en: Write this down and keep it somewhere safe and separate from your phone. If your Face ID or device passcode ever changes and locks you out, this code plus your PIN restores your messages. We can't show it again.

protection_recovery_entry_subtitle.en: Enter the recovery code you saved plus your %1$s. This restores your messages. If this phone can still use the hardware lock, it switches back on with this same code, so keep the code safe.

protection_recovery_generic_error.en: Couldn’t recover right now — no recovery code on file, or the device key is busy. Try again.

protection_recovery_wrong_credential.en: That code and %1$s didn’t match. Check both and try again.

protection_stop_no_biometrics.en: Biometrics is missing. setup Face ID or fingerprint.

protection_stop_no_chip.en: This phone has no security chip.

protection_stop_no_lock.en: Your phone has no %1$s, only Maximum can protect Rún here.

protection_tier_tagline_casual.en: Six digit pin code for opening Rún. Can be brute forced by forensic tools in hours, so Rún relies fully on the phone protection. On Android, keyboard suggestions and emoji stay on, so the keyboard may learn words you type.

protection_tier_tagline_maximum.en: A long passphrase instead of a pin code — strong enough that no forensic tool can brute force it, even from an unlocked phone. The keyboard runs in password mode: nothing you type is learned or suggested, and on Android the emoji key is unavailable.

protection_tier_tagline_private.en: Six digit pin code, but the vault key is sealed in the phone's security chip and released only by your fingerprint or face. A seized phone resists forensic brute-forcing even if its passcode is cracked. On Android, keyboard suggestions and emoji stay on, so the keyboard may learn words you type.

protection_title.en: Choose protection level against forensic attacks

push_prompt_message.en: Do you want to enable push notifications?

referral_introduce_body.en: Select who to introduce %1$s to. Only introduce people you know and trust.

referral_introduce_error.en: Not connected yet — try again in a moment.

referral_offer_message.en: %1$s wants to introduce you to “%2$s”. Approve to add them as a contact.

referral_relayed_complete.en: Both %1$s and %2$s approved. Each now has what they need to reach the other. You have no part in their conversation and cannot read it.

referral_relayed_first.en: %1$s approved your introduction to %2$s. Their connection details have been passed on. Once %2$s approves too, they can message each other.

referral_relayed_queued.en: %1$s approved your introduction to %2$s. Rún could not reach the relay just now and will pass their details on automatically next time you open the app.

report_abuse_email_body.en:
I want to report a contact for objectionable content or abusive behaviour.

Contact (the name I gave them on my device): %1$s

What happened (please describe in your own words):


---
Rún reviews every report within 24 hours and acts on it — barring abusive
senders where technically possible and reporting illegal content to the
appropriate authorities.

This email is stored by your mail app, outside Rún's encrypted storage, so
please include only what you are comfortable keeping there.

report_bug_failed.en: Couldn't send the report — check the connection and try again.

report_bug_placeholder.en: What happened, and what did you expect?

report_bug_thanks.en: Thank you for helping to improve Rún

report_email_fallback_message.en: No email app is set up on this device. Tap Copy report, then paste it into any email addressed to %1$s.

settings_language_restart_message.en: Rún needs to restart to switch the app's language to %1$s. Continue?

setup_choose_body.en: Already using Rún on another phone? Move it here and your contacts, groups and conversations come with you.

terms_contact_enforcement.en: Reports are acted on within 24 hours: offending content is removed and abusive users are ejected.

tip_appeal.en: Rún has no ads, no investors, and never sells your data. A tip — any size — helps keep it free and independent.

tip_error_checkout_failed.en: Couldn't open Google Play checkout. Try again.

tip_error_purchase_failed.en: Tip didn't go through. Try again.

tip_error_unavailable_device.en: In-app tips aren't available on this device.

tip_store_disclosure.en: Processed by the App Store · ties to your Apple ID · no other third party.

tip_thank_you_body.en: Your support keeps Rún free and independent.
